takeaway: Milroy disease is a congenital, hereditary primary lymphoedema (aplasia of the lymph trunks); surgery, radiotherapy, cancer and TB are secondary causes.

question.text: Which one of the following conditions is a cause of primary lymphoedema?
question.say: Which one of the following conditions is a cause of primary lymphoedema?

lines.text: Primary lymphoedema has no outside cause.
Milroy disease is the classic example: congenital and hereditary.
The child is born with a swollen leg.
The lymph trunks of the leg never formed: aplasia, a closed gate, so the lymph cannot drain.
Swelling slowly progresses in one or both legs.
Secondary lymphoedema is different: surgery, radiotherapy, cancer or tuberculosis damage normal lymphatics.
So the primary cause is Milroy disease.
